note: Every MCP server adds tool definitions to the agent context, and they count against Antigravity's 20,000-token customization budget (check with eag budget). Add only the servers you use. eag mcp add <name> previews by default and writes only with --yes, after backing up your mcp_config.json. Remote servers use the url key; community servers are marked and reviewed for scope, but read their security note first.

chrome-devtools.description: Chrome DevTools for agents: performance traces, network, console, Lighthouse-style insights.
chrome-devtools.when: Diagnosing web performance (LCP/INP/CLS), network errors and console failures.

playwright.description: Browser automation through Playwright with accessibility-tree snapshots.
playwright.when: Scripted E2E exploration outside Antigravity's built-in browser, or in Gemini CLI.

aws.description: AWS MCP Server (managed) via the SigV4 proxy: call AWS APIs, run guided agent workflows, search AWS docs.
aws.when: Operate or inspect AWS resources from the agent using your AWS profile.
aws.security: Can call any API the profile allows; use a read-only IAM role (proxy supports --read-only) and never root credentials.

azure.description: Azure MCP Server: storage, Cosmos DB, Key Vault, AKS, App Service, Monitor, resource groups and more.
azure.security: Uses your signed-in Azure identity, including Key Vault secret reads; sign in with a least-privilege account.

cloudflare.description: Cloudflare Workers Bindings MCP: manage Workers, KV, R2, D1 and Hyperdrive. Sibling hosted servers: docs.mcp.cloudflare.com (no auth) and observability.mcp.cloudflare.com.
cloudflare.when: Build or debug on Cloudflare's developer platform.
cloudflare.security: OAuth can delete KV namespaces, R2 buckets and D1 databases; pick a non-production account.

docker.description: Docker MCP Gateway: one stdio endpoint that runs containerized servers enabled in Docker Desktop's MCP Toolkit catalog.
docker.when: Run many MCP servers isolated in containers with centrally managed secrets.
docker.security: Exposes every server enabled in your profile; use --profile to limit; containers reduce but do not remove host risk.

firebase.description: Firebase CLI MCP server (projects, apps, rules, deploy status). Antigravity also has an official Firebase plugin.
firebase.when: Firebase work from Gemini CLI, or when you prefer the CLI server over the plugin.

gcloud.description: Google gcloud MCP: run gcloud CLI commands through natural language across Google Cloud services.
gcloud.when: Broad Google Cloud administration from the agent.
gcloud.security: Runs gcloud as your account, which can delete resources; use a restricted configuration or service account.

kubernetes.description: Kubernetes/OpenShift MCP (native Go, no kubectl needed): pods, logs, exec, resources, events, Helm.
kubernetes.when: Inspect or debug clusters from the agent.
kubernetes.security: Acts with your current kube context; set read_only = true / disable_destructive = true in a TOML file passed via --config, and rely on RBAC.

terraform.description: HashiCorp Terraform MCP: Registry provider, module and policy docs, plus HCP Terraform/TFE workspace operations.
terraform.when: Write correct Terraform using current provider docs; manage HCP Terraform runs.
terraform.security: TFE_TOKEN is optional (registry tools work without it) and can trigger runs; use a team token scoped to non-prod workspaces.

vercel.description: Vercel hosted MCP: projects, deployments, build and runtime logs, domains and docs search.
vercel.when: Diagnose failed deployments or inspect Vercel projects.
vercel.security: OAuth inherits team permissions; logs may contain secrets or PII.

serena.description: Serena: LSP-backed semantic code navigation and symbol-level editing for 30+ languages.
serena.when: Large codebases where symbol search and references beat grep. Install first: uv tool install -p 3.13 serena-agent.
serena.security: Edits files and can run shell commands; its docs warn against marketplace installs. Activate only the intended project.

snyk.description: Snyk MCP (part of the Snyk CLI): SAST, open-source dependency, IaC and container scans from the agent.
snyk.when: Security-scan generated code and dependencies before commit.
snyk.security: Uploads code snippets or manifests to Snyk for analysis; check org data policies.

bigquery.description: Google-managed BigQuery remote MCP: list datasets and tables, read schemas, run SQL queries.
bigquery.when: Analytics on BigQuery from the agent without running a local server.
bigquery.security: Needs roles/mcp.toolUser, bigquery.jobUser, bigquery.dataViewer; queries bill the project; use a dedicated agent identity.

mongodb.description: MongoDB MCP: query, aggregate, inspect schemas and indexes; optional Atlas cluster management.
mongodb.security: Connection string is a secret; --readOnly blocks writes; Atlas API credentials can create clusters and users.

neon.description: Neon hosted MCP: projects, branches, SQL, schema migrations on branches, query tuning.
neon.when: Serverless Postgres on Neon, especially branch-per-change migration workflows.
neon.security: OAuth can create or delete projects and branches; review migrations before applying to main.

postgres.description: PostgreSQL via Google MCP Toolbox prebuilt tools: list schemas and tables, run SQL, explain queries.
postgres.when: Any Postgres database; replaces the archived @modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres.
postgres.security: execute_sql runs any statement; connect with a read-only role or use --prebuilt=postgres/<toolset> to limit tools.

prisma.description: Prisma hosted MCP: create and manage Prisma Postgres databases, run migrations, manage Prisma Compute apps.
prisma.when: Projects on Prisma Postgres. The local `npx prisma mcp` was removed in Prisma 8.
prisma.security: OAuth account can create and delete databases; confirm destructive migrations.

redis.description: Redis MCP: read and write strings, hashes, lists, sets, streams, JSON and vector search indexes.
redis.when: Inspect caches, queues or vector indexes in Redis.
redis.security: No read-only mode: tools can delete keys. A password inside --url shows in process lists; prefer the REDIS_PWD env var.

sqlite.description: SQLite via Google MCP Toolbox prebuilt tools: list tables and run SQL on a local database file.
sqlite.when: Local SQLite files; replaces the archived reference mcp-server-sqlite.
sqlite.security: SQL tools can modify or drop tables; work on a copy of important database files.

supabase.description: Supabase hosted MCP: tables, SQL, migrations, edge functions, logs, branches and docs search.
supabase.when: Apps backed by Supabase Postgres, auth and storage.
supabase.security: Without read_only=true the agent can run DDL/DML; scope to a dev project via project_ref, never production.

figma.description: Figma hosted MCP: design context, variables, components, screenshots and Code Connect for selected frames.
figma.when: Implement UI from Figma designs with accurate tokens and layout.
figma.security: OAuth reads every file you can access; rate limits depend on Figma seat type.

next-devtools.description: Next.js DevTools MCP: connects to a running Next.js 16+ dev server for runtime errors, routes, logs and version-matched docs.
next-devtools.security: Talks to local dev servers only; low risk.

shadcn.description: shadcn/ui MCP: browse, search and install components and blocks from shadcn and other configured registries.
shadcn.security: Installs code from registries in components.json; review third-party registries before adding them.

aws-knowledge.description: AWS Knowledge: AWS docs search, API references, What's New, regional availability and best-practice guidance.
aws-knowledge.when: Grounding AWS architecture or SDK answers; no AWS account needed.
aws-knowledge.security: Public docs only, no credentials; rate limited.

context7.description: Up-to-date library and framework documentation lookup (resolve a library, then query its docs).
context7.when: You work with fast-moving libraries and want current APIs instead of training-data guesses.

deepwiki.description: DeepWiki (Cognition): AI-generated docs and Q&A for any public GitHub repository.
deepwiki.when: Understand an unfamiliar open-source dependency's architecture or API without cloning it.
deepwiki.security: Public repos only; questions are sent to a third party, so keep private code out of prompts.

google-developer-knowledge.description: Google Developer Knowledge: search and retrieve official docs for Firebase, Google Cloud, Android, Maps and more.
google-developer-knowledge.when: Current Google product docs; the firebase entry may already expose these tools, so add only if missing.
google-developer-knowledge.security: Restrict the API key to the Developer Knowledge API; never pass the key as a URL query parameter.

huggingface.description: Hugging Face Hub: search models, datasets, Spaces and papers, read docs, and call Gradio Spaces as tools.
huggingface.when: Choosing models or datasets, or reading HF library docs.
huggingface.security: Use a read-only HF token; Space tools run third-party code remotely.

microsoft-learn.description: Microsoft Learn docs search, fetch and official code samples for Azure, .NET, M365 and Windows.
microsoft-learn.when: Grounding answers about Microsoft and Azure APIs in current official documentation.
microsoft-learn.security: Read-only public docs; no credentials; low risk.

datadog.description: Datadog hosted MCP: logs, metrics, traces, monitors, incidents, dashboards and notebooks.
datadog.when: Teams on Datadog investigating errors or performance. Endpoint is per site (US1 shown).
datadog.security: OAuth recommended; for headers use a scoped service-account app key. Not supported on GovCloud sites.

grafana.description: Grafana MCP: search dashboards, query Prometheus/Loki/datasources, alerts, incidents and OnCall.
grafana.when: Investigate metrics and logs during debugging or incident response.
grafana.security: Use a Viewer-role service account; --disable-write blocks dashboard/alert edits; drop it only when writes are needed.

posthog.description: PostHog hosted MCP: product analytics queries, feature flags, experiments, error tracking and insights.
posthog.when: Check flag state, query usage data or error tracking while building features.
posthog.security: Can create or flip feature flags in production; use a scoped personal API key or read-only scopes.

sentry.description: Sentry hosted MCP: issues, events, stack traces, releases, traces and Seer root-cause analysis.
sentry.when: Debug production errors: fetch the issue and stack trace, then fix the code.
sentry.security: OAuth spans all orgs you belong to; error payloads may contain PII and untrusted user input.

paypal.description: PayPal hosted MCP: invoices, orders, payments, subscriptions, disputes, shipment tracking and reporting.
paypal.when: Integrate or operate PayPal commerce flows.
paypal.security: Live accounts can send invoices and issue refunds; use the sandbox environment for development.

stripe.description: Stripe hosted MCP: search the Stripe API, read and write objects (customers, prices, invoices, refunds) and search docs.
stripe.when: Build or debug Stripe integrations; prefer a sandbox account.
stripe.security: Can create refunds and move money; use OAuth on a sandbox or an agent API key (Bearer header). Full secret keys are rejected from 2027-01-11.

atlassian.description: Atlassian Rovo hosted MCP for Jira, Confluence and Compass: search, create and update issues and pages.
atlassian.when: Teams tracking work in Jira or specs in Confluence.
atlassian.security: OAuth inherits your Jira/Confluence permissions incl. writes; site admins can restrict access. Ticket text is untrusted input.

github.description: GitHub's remote MCP server (issues, PRs, repos, actions).
github.when: Repository automation beyond what the `gh` CLI covers.

gitlab.description: GitLab built-in MCP server: issues, merge requests, pipelines, search and project data.
gitlab.when: Repos hosted on GitLab.com or self-managed GitLab (replace host).
gitlab.security: OAuth token with mcp scope or fine-grained PAT; legacy PATs are rejected. Admins must allow MCP for the group or instance.

linear.description: Linear hosted MCP: find, create and update issues, projects, cycles and comments.
linear.when: Agent works tickets end to end: read an issue, implement, update status.
linear.security: OAuth grants your full workspace write access; use https://mcp.linear.app/mcp/readonly for read-only agents.

notion.description: Notion hosted MCP: search, read, create and update pages and databases.
notion.when: Pull specs or notes from Notion, or write status and docs back.
notion.security: OAuth covers every page you can see; for the local server, share only needed pages with the integration.

slack.description: Community Slack MCP: read channels, threads and DMs, search messages; posting is opt-in.
slack.when: Pull discussion context from Slack. Slack's official https://mcp.slack.com/mcp needs a registered Slack app (no dynamic client registration).
slack.security: User token reads everything you can; keep SLACK_MCP_ADD_MESSAGE_TOOL off; avoid its xoxc/xoxd browser-cookie mode (may breach workspace policy).

memory.description: Local knowledge-graph memory (entities, relations, observations) persisted to a JSON file.
memory.when: You want structured long-term memory in addition to EAG instincts and session summaries.

sequential-thinking.when: Long multi-step design or debugging sessions where explicit thought revision helps.

fetch.description: Fetch a URL and convert HTML to markdown, with chunked reads for long pages (MCP reference server, Python).
fetch.when: Read docs, changelogs or API pages by URL when the client has no web-fetch tool.
fetch.security: Can reach localhost and internal hosts (SSRF); restrict with --allowed-hosts and treat fetched pages as untrusted (prompt injection).

filesystem.description: Read, write, search, move and list files inside explicitly allowed directories (MCP reference server).
filesystem.when: Agent needs file access outside its built-in workspace tools, or a client has no native file tools.
filesystem.security: Write/move/edit tools can overwrite anything under the allowed dirs; list only project dirs, never home or drive root.

git.description: Git status, diff, log, branch, checkout, add, commit and reset on a local repository (MCP reference server, Python).
git.when: Structured git operations for clients without a shell tool, or to scope git access to one repo.
git.security: Can commit, reset and switch branches; scope --repository to one repo and review commits before pushing.

time.description: Current time and timezone conversion using IANA zones (MCP reference server, Python).
time.when: Scheduling, log correlation or date math where the model must not guess the current time.
time.security: Read-only, no network or credentials; low risk.

apify.description: Apify hosted MCP: run thousands of Apify Store Actors for scraping, extraction and browser automation.
apify.when: Site-specific scrapers (maps, social, e-commerce) that a generic fetch cannot handle.
apify.security: Token grants full Apify account access and Actors run on paid compute; pick a minimal tool set and check scraping terms.

brave-search.description: Brave Search API: web, news, image, video and local search plus AI summaries.
brave-search.when: General web search with an independent index; replaces the archived @modelcontextprotocol/server-brave-search.
brave-search.security: API key is billable; search results are untrusted web content (prompt injection).

exa.description: Exa neural web search, code-context search, page contents and deep research (hosted).
exa.when: Semantic web or code-example search; works without a key on a rate-limited free tier.
exa.security: Queries go to Exa; do not put an API key in the URL query string; results are untrusted content.

firecrawl.description: Firecrawl scrape, crawl, map, search and structured extraction from websites.
firecrawl.when: Turn whole sites or JS-heavy pages into markdown or JSON for the agent.
firecrawl.security: Crawls consume credits fast; set crawl limits; scraped content is untrusted (prompt injection).

tavily.description: Tavily search, extract, map and crawl tuned for LLM agents.
tavily.when: Agentic research needing search plus clean page extraction in one tool set.
tavily.security: Billable API key; avoid the documented ?tavilyApiKey= URL form, which leaks the key into logs.
